local.h: Brookline residents report owl attacks
local.b: More than two dozen people in Brookline believe they've been attacked by the same owl.
local.title: Spate of reported owl attacks strikes Brookline

local.h: Baystate resumes gender care for youth
local.b: Baystate Health will again prescribe gender-affirming medication for minors starting Dec. 15, almost a year after halting the program amid threats from Washington.
local.title: Baystate resumes gender care for youth, after shutting it down amid government threats

local.h: Harvard: Data center emissions far worse than thought
local.b: A Harvard study of 403 large data centers found their climate pollution is three times greater than previously estimated.

local.h: Beacon Hill welcomes at least 21 new lawmakers
local.b: The incoming class includes a 19-year-old from Billerica, a 'Bachelorette' contestant and the sitting mayor of Gardner; every freshman but one is a Democrat.

local.h: Massachusetts sues ICE over courthouse arrests
local.b: Attorney General Andrea Campbell sued the Trump administration, saying immigration agents keep arresting people inside Massachusetts courthouses in violation of a new state law.

local.h: Coastal storm set to soak Thanksgiving
local.b: Tuesday and Wednesday look clear for travel, but a coastal storm is expected to bring soaking rain, strong wind gusts and coastal flooding on Thanksgiving Day.

goodnews.b: The EPA reached agreements with state conservation officials and 54 other parties to advance a $78.6 million cleanup of decades of industrial pollution in the Lower Neponset River.

goodnews.h: Skatesgiving brings roller skating and turkeys to Dorchester
goodnews.b: Kids skated in the Joseph Lee K-8 School auditorium Friday night at an annual community event where families also picked up Thanksgiving food.

goodnews.h: ProBlak's mural brings community stories to A.R.T.'s new center
goodnews.b: Artist Rob "ProBlak" Gibbs has created a massive mural for the American Repertory Theater's new Goel Center in Allston, which opens to the public in April 2027.

local.h: Bill would let assault survivors sue colleges
local.b: Illinois lawmakers are weighing a proposal letting campus sexual assault survivors sue universities that fail to provide supports required by state law.
local.title: Illinois legislation could help more survivors of campus sexual assault stay in college

local.h: Top cop finalist was disciplined three times
local.b: Records show CPD counterterrorism chief Christopher Papaioannou, a superintendent finalist, was suspended or reprimanded three times and drew dozens of complaints.

local.h: Workers walk out at Humboldt Park coffee shop
local.b: Tasa Coffee Roasters faces boycott calls and was egged after a viral post alleged ties to ICE; workers walked off the job Monday.
local.title: Latino-focused Tasa Coffee Roasters targeted by social media post alleging ties to ICE

local.h: NW Indiana food banks see heavy need
local.b: After a year of storms and cuts to SNAP benefits, Northwest Indiana is leaning on its food banks ahead of Thanksgiving.

local.h: Chicago crime falls, domestic violence rises
local.b: While overall crime is dropping in Chicago, domestic violence is getting worse; experts and survivors discuss what it would take to reduce it.

local.h: Chicago bets on the Soul Train Awards to boost tourism
local.b: Taped in Chicago, the Soul Train Awards return to network TV Friday after a two-year hiatus, and local officials hope the show will draw tourism and more awards specials to the city.

local.h: Ankle monitors take over a Chicagoan's life
local.b: As the administration puts ankle monitors on more immigrants, advocates say they aren't necessary for people complying with their cases and take a toll on mental health.

goodnews.h: Druski to host Chicago's New Year's Eve
goodnews.b: The comedian will host the city's celebration from Navy Pier, broadcast live; free tickets go out first-come, first-served starting Wednesday.
goodnews.title: Druski to host Chicago New Year’s Eve celebration and live TV broadcast from Navy Pier

local.h: Denver approves $40M DNC standby fund
local.b: The city will provide a $40 million financial guarantee for its bid to host the Democratic National Convention.
local.title: Denver approves $40M of ‘standby’ funding for Democratic National Convention

local.h: Denver in the mix for 2031 Women's World Cup
local.b: The 2031 Women's World Cup is coming to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, and Denver is in the mix to host games.
local.title: Denver is in the mix to host games for the 2031 Women’s World Cup

local.h: Saturday flurries weren't Denver's first snow
local.b: The weekend flurries didn't count as Denver's official first snow, making this already the third-latest first snow on record.
local.title: Sorry, those Saturday flurries didn’t count as Denver’s official first snow

local.h: California port pollution rule faces Congress
local.b: Republicans in Congress are trying to revoke a California rule targeting smog from ships idling at the ports of LA and Long Beach.
local.title: This neon green barge is part of how California is cutting port pollution. Will Congress interfere?

local.h: Judge orders search of LA city attorney's devices
local.b: A judge ordered a forensic search of Hydee Feldstein Soto's devices for messages about a former prosecutor who says she was fired for reporting alleged illegal conduct.
local.title: Judge sanctions outgoing LA city attorney, orders forensic search of her devices

local.h: Fight over 20,000 California ballots ends
local.b: A federal appeals court approved the Justice Department's bid to drop its own suit that sought to pause the counting of roughly 20,000 ballots.
local.title: Legal fight over 20,000 California ballots ends as appeals court OKs DOJ dismissal

local.h: High gas prices cancel some holiday trips
local.b: Gas prices in the LA-Long Beach area fell about 60 cents in the last month, AAA says, but some drivers have still canceled Thanksgiving travel.
local.title: Gasoline prices may be inching down, but some have already canceled Thanksgiving travel plans

local.h: LA weighs rent freeze for seniors, disabled
local.b: Councilmember Ysabel Jurado introduced a motion to explore a program that would keep rents flat for qualifying tenants.
local.title: LA considers taxpayer-funded rent freeze for some senior and disabled tenants

local.h: UC gives all students ChatGPT access
local.b: The University of California signed a $1.2 million deal with OpenAI for ChatGPT Edu, despite faculty concerns that they weren't sufficiently consulted.
local.title: UC gives students free access to ChatGPT. Faculty say OpenAI deal is ‘unwise’

local.h: Thanksgiving dinner may cost more this year
local.b: The American Farm Bureau Federation estimates Thanksgiving will cost more than 6% more than last year, though other food-price experts say the increase is unclear.

local.h: Ethics panel finds Rep. Gomez made unwelcome advances
local.b: The House Ethics Committee reported 'substantial evidence' that Rep. Jimmy Gomez made unwelcome sexual advances and contact toward a House staffer.

local.h: Woman stabbed at random in Riverside Park
local.b: Police are searching for a man who stabbed a 26-year-old woman near West 96th Street Monday night; she is in stable condition.
local.title: NYPD searches for suspect who police say stabbed a woman at random in Riverside Park

local.h: Lawsuit says co-signer firm inflates rents
local.b: A class action accuses TheGuarantors of raising renters' costs through exclusive deals with landlords that block cheaper options.
local.title: NYC renters face ‘higher fees, reduced housing access’ due to co-signer company, lawsuit says

local.h: Report backs regular taxi fare hikes
local.b: A Taxi and Limousine Commission report says yellow cab operating costs rose about 16% since 2022, and regular fare hikes could help drivers avoid poverty.
local.title: Fare hikes on yellow taxi cabs could keep drivers out of poverty, city report finds

local.h: Hochul vetoes AI accuracy-warning bill
local.b: Gov. Kathy Hochul vetoed a bill requiring AI platforms to warn users their information may be inaccurate, calling it too far-reaching.
local.title: NY Gov. Hochul vetoes bill that would have required AI accuracy warnings

local.h: Queens library restores most services
local.b: Nearly three weeks after a Nov. 4 ransomware attack, the Queens Public Library has its website, app, computers and digital collections back up.
local.title: Queens Public Library restores most services nearly 3 weeks after ransomware attack

local.h: Flu cases surge ahead of Thanksgiving
local.b: More than 43,000 New Yorkers have caught the flu since early October, compared with about 7,000 at this point last season, state data shows.
local.title: Reported flu cases surge across New York ahead of Thanksgiving

local.h: NY sues HUD over mixed-status housing rule
local.b: The state and city sued over a federal rule that could strip housing assistance from about 20,000 families in which not every member is a citizen or eligible non-citizen.
local.title: NYC, state sue Trump administration over ‘mixed-status’ federal housing assistance rule

local.h: Top court upholds Section 8 renter protection
local.b: New York's Court of Appeals upheld a state law banning discrimination against tenants who pay rent with housing subsidies, siding with Attorney General Letitia James against an Ithaca landlord.
local.title: New York’s highest court upholds key protection for low-income renters with Section 8

local.h: New film captures ICE agents' banter at NYC courthouse arrests
local.b: Journalist Emma V.F. filmed scores of arrests at 26 Federal Plaza, along with the rarely seen small talk among the ICE agents making them.
local.title: New film captures ICE agents' banter amid NYC courthouse arrests

local.h: Citi Bike e-bike rides to be capped at $3.65 for members
local.b: Under a new deal between Mayor Zohran Mamdani's administration and Lyft, Citi Bike members will pay no more than $3.65 for e-bike rides up to 45 minutes starting Jan. 19, 2027.
local.title: NYC Citi Bike member rides to be capped at $3.65 after Mamdani inks new deal with Lyft

goodnews.b: Green-Wood Cemetery fellows are sifting soil to catalogue potentially thousands of unknown fungus species.
goodnews.title: Digging up a secret world under a Brooklyn graveyard, one teaspoon at a time

goodnews.h: About 100 New Yorkers ditched their smartphones for a month
goodnews.b: A phone-free party celebrated roughly 100 New Yorkers who gave up their smartphones for a month, with a showcase of the hobbies and art projects they picked up instead.
goodnews.title: These New Yorkers ditched their smartphones for a month. No, seriously.

local.h: Freezing temperatures hit France
local.b: Arctic air is bringing a sharp drop in temperatures, with overnight lows below freezing in several regions this week.

local.h: Map shows France's hardest tap water
local.b: Tap water hardness varies significantly across France, and hard water builds limescale on taps and kettles and can dry out skin and hair.

local.h: Three detained over Normandy train derailment
local.b: French police arrested three people in connection with the September derailment between Rouen and Caen that injured 44 people, sources said.

local.h: Where the presidential candidates stand on rural France
local.b: Rural France, home to a third of the population, is a key 2027 battleground, with residents more reliant on cars and facing reduced public services such as healthcare. A look at the candidates' policies.

goodnews.b: A young French chef won the world championship of œuf mayonnaise in Saint-Ouen-sur-Seine, where competitors each made 100 eggs.
goodnews.title: '8 minutes and 40 seconds for perfection'

local.h: Seattle schools settle over pregnant workers
local.b: Seattle Public Schools will pay $600,000 and revise policies for pregnant and nursing employees under a settlement with the state attorney general.

local.h: King tides could break records this week
local.b: El Niño-heated water along the West Coast could push this week's king tides to record highs, forecasters expect.

local.h: Seattle schools require sex attestation for girls sports
local.b: The district is asking families to complete a 'biological sex attestation' form to comply with Initiative 638, which bans trans girls from girls sports.

local.h: Dallesport residents fight huge data center plan
local.b: Neighbors in rural Klickitat County are organizing against a proposed hyperscale data center campus that could one day reach one gigawatt.

local.h: Longest-serving state justice to retire
local.b: Washington Supreme Court Justice Charles W. Johnson, on the court for 36 years, will leave when his term ends this year at the state's mandatory age limit of 75.

local.h: Seattle lab aims to break down 'forever chemicals'
local.b: Nature has no tools to break down PFAS, the so-called forever chemicals invented in the 1930s. A Seattle protein design lab is trying to build some.
